pack.title: Try the study flow
pack.description: One fictional observation exercise demonstrates the pack format. Import your own material from Study packs.

tracks.title: Sample
tracks.description: A short fictional example for exploring the app.

sessions.title: Describe a fictional scene
sessions.capability: Separate an observation from a guess
sessions.prompt: A fictional scene contains a blue cup on a table. Which statement describes only what you can see?
options: A blue cup stands on a table.
sessions.feedback: The scene gives a cup, its colour and its position. It gives no information about a drink or a person.
sessions.model: Describe visible details before adding interpretations. If you make a guess, label it as a guess.
sessions.example: Observation: a blue cup stands on a table. Guess: someone left it after breakfast.
sessions.trigger: You want another person to know which details came from the scene.
sessions.nonTrigger: An imaginative story can add invented details when you label it as fiction.
sessions.invariant: Keep observed details separate from invented explanations.

trace.note: List the details supplied in the fictional scene.
Mark an explanation as a guess because the scene does not establish it.

decision.prompt: The description adds that the cup is empty. How should you treat that detail?
options: As a guess unless the scene shows the inside.
As certain because cups are often empty.
decision.feedback: The supplied scene does not show the inside of the cup.

sessions.explainPrompt: Use a different invented object to explain the difference between an observation and a guess.
checklist: I labelled my added explanation as a guess.
rubric: Describe two details in a fictional scene.
Label one invented explanation as a guess.
sessions.reviewPrompt: Which details would you need to check before calling a guess an observation?
sessions.task: Invent a scene with two objects. Write two observations and one labelled guess. This is a sample for exploring the app, not a course.
